deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This page continues a table that begins on the previous page (193, 233, 241, 257). For each prime p ≡ 1 (mod 4) it records the class group of properly primitive binary forms ax²+2bxy+cy² of determinant −p (discriminant −4p, Disquisitiones notation). It also records the link between the principal genus and the decompositions of p into three squares (Disq. Arith. art. 291–292). The next page ('Caput 3. Primi bis sumti') does the same for determinants −2p.

LAYOUT OF EACH ENTRY.
- Braced array 0 1 … h/2−1 over h h−1 … h/2+1, with h/2 written alone. Gauss has chosen a generating class 'Cl.1', so the group is cyclic of order h with classes numbered by exponent k = 0, 1, …, h−1.
- Class k is paired with its inverse h−k. Class 0 is the principal class; class h/2 is the non-principal ambiguous class (the form (2,1,(p+1)/2)).
- 'c.' stands for 'continet' (contains). The small primes after it are primes properly represented by forms of that class. For example, 'Cl.1.19 c. 3.127' means 3 and 127 lie in classes 1 and 19.
- Even-indexed classes form the principal genus. Each inverse pair {2k, h−2k}, and each self-inverse class 0 and h/2, carries one essentially distinct representation p = x²+y²+z². Class 0 carries the one with a zero term; class h/2 carries the one with two equal squares.

CONSISTENCY CHECK (mine). Let N = number of essentially distinct decompositions of p into three squares, which equals 1 + (h/4 − 1) + 1 = h/4 + 1. Then r3(p) = 24·2 + 48·(N−2) = 12h. This is the Gauss relation r3(n) = 12·h(−4n) for squarefree n ≡ 1, 2 (mod 4).

p = 281, h = 20.
- Cl0: 256+25 = 16²+5²+0².
- Cl2/18: 4+81+196 (2,9,14).
- Cl4/16: 16+121+144 (4,11,12).
- Cl6/14: 36+49+196 (6,7,14).
- Cl8/12: 9+16+256 (3,4,16).
- Cl10: 100+100+81 (10,10,9).
- r3(281) = 24 + 4·48 + 24 = 240 = 12·20.
- Primes:
  - 3 and 127 lie in classes 1/19. 3 is represented by (3,1,94). For 127, (127,10,3) reduces to (3,−1,94), the inverse of (3,1,94).
  - 19 lies in class 5/15. Its form (15,−2,19) squares to (225,13,2) ~ (2,1,141), the ambiguous class 10, so it has order 4, as an index 5 requires.
  - 5 lies in class 6/14, via (5,2,57).
  - My check: with g = (3,1,94), g⁴ ~ (10,±3,29) and (5,2,57)² ~ (17,5,18), (5,2,57)⁴ ~ (10,3,29). This is consistent with (5-form) = g^{±6}.
  - Genus characters fit. 3, 19 and 127 are ≡ 3 mod 4 and quadratic non-residues mod 281, so they lie in the odd-index genus. 5 is ≡ 1 mod 4 and a residue mod 281, so it lies in the principal genus.

p = 401, h = 20.
- Cl0: 400+1 (20,1,0).
- Cl2/18: 196+169+36 (14,13,6).

- Cl6/14: 361+36+4 (19,6,2).

- 5 lies in class 4/16, via (5,2,81), a class of order 5.
- The entry breaks off after 'Cl.7.13. c'. The complete list of decompositions (my enumeration) also contains (16,12,1) and (14,14,3). These would fill Cl8/12 = 256+144+1 and Cl10 = 196+196+9.
- Full count: 24+4·48+24 = 240 = 12·20.
errors: No arithmetic errors: every three-square decomposition on the page sums to the stated prime.
Every stated class number agrees with r3(p) = 12h: 281→20, 313→8, 337→8, 353→16, 401→20.
The 401 entry is incomplete: classes 8/12, 9/11 and 10 are missing. They should be 256+144+1 (Cl8/12) and 196+196+9 (Cl10).
The 401 Cl.6.14 entry is overwritten in the manuscript; the only value consistent with p is 361+36+4.
Minor inconsistency only: 'c.' is omitted after the 313 Cl.2.6 and Cl.4 entries and after 401 Cl.2.18.

results.what: Class numbers and cyclic class-group structure of properly primitive forms of determinant −p for p = 281, 313, 337, 353, 401 (h = 20, 8, 8, 16, 20), with classes indexed as powers of a generator.
results.modern_name: Class group Cl(−4p), cyclic case; tables of class numbers
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (Disquisitiones Arithmeticae 1801, art. 305–306; class-number tables in Werke II)

results.what: Correspondence between principal-genus classes (modulo inversion) and essentially distinct representations p = x²+y²+z², equivalently r3(p) = 12·h(−4p).
results.modern_name: Gauss's three-squares theorem / class-number formula for r3(n)

results.what: Assignment of small primes (3, 5, 17, 19, 127) to classes, consistent with genus characters and composition (e.g. the 19-class in determinant −281 has order 4).
results.modern_name: Genus theory / location of prime ideals in the class group

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine computational tabulation of material Gauss published in the Disquisitiones: cyclic class groups of determinant −p, genus structure, and the three-square correspondence. Similar class-number tables from his Nachlass are known. The only notable feature is the explicit indexing of classes by powers of a generator.

checkable.asserts: All decompositions listed for 281 are correct.
The decompositions for 313 and 337 are correct.
The decompositions for 353 and 401 are correct, including the two missing 401 entries.

checkable.asserts: The number of reduced properly primitive forms ax^2+2bxy+cy^2 of determinant -p equals the class numbers on the page (uses gcd from sympy).

checkable.asserts: The listed primes lie in the genera implied by the parity of their class index.
The forms used are valid for determinant -p. (15,-2,19) squared gives (225,13,2) ~ (2,1,141), so the 19-class has order 4, matching index 5 of 20.
